'''Myrkr''' was a [[Forest/Legends|forested]] [[Planet/Legends|world]], located fairly close to [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy's]] major population centers in the outskirts of the [[Inner Rim/Legends|Inner Rim]] Territories. It was close to the borders with the [[Expansion Region/Legends|Expansion Region]] and relatively near to the planet of [[Wayland/Legends|Wayland]]. It was believed to be the [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of the [[Neti/Legends|Neti]] species, although the Neti established a colony on [[Ryyk]] some time prior to [[4000 BBY/Legends|4000 BBY]], apparently abandoning Myrkr.

Since the planet attracted little attention, it was frequently visited by [[Smuggler/Legends|smugglers]], fugitives and all kinds of other outlaws, which were known to build secret bases in the depths of Myrkr's forests.

==Description==
[[File:Ysalamiri_tree.jpg|thumb|left|150px|Native [[Ysalamiri/Legends|Ysalamiri]].]]
Myrkr was primarily a [[Forest/Legends|forested]] world, located in the [[Myrkr system/Legends|Myrkr system]] of the [[Inner Rim/Legends|Inner Rim]] Territories. Its forests were home to the [[Ysalamiri/Legends|ysalamiri]] lizard-like creatures, which were known to posses the ability to "push back" [[The Force/Legends|the Force]]. Other indigenous animals that were present on the planet's surface included the [[vornskr]], a deadly whip-tailed creature which used the energy field of the Force to hunt and track its prey.<ref name="EGPM">''[[The Essential Guide to Planets and Moons]]''</ref>

The planet also possessed unique trees, which were known to have a high metal content and systematically interfered with many [[Sensor/Legends|sensor]] scan devices.<ref name="EGPM" />

Myrkr's forested surface also had some urban areas like the unobtrusive port town of [[Hyllyard City]]. Although it served as the largest urban settlement and the commercial hub of the planet, its inhabitants mostly consisted of smugglers, malcontents and fugitives from other worlds.<ref name="TCSWE">''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''</ref>

==History==
The planet was first discovered between [[20,000 BBY/Legends|20,000 BBY]] to [[15,000 BBY/Legends|15,000 BBY]], sometime between the [[Great Manifest Period/Legends|Great Manifest Period]] and the settlement of [[Trailing Sectors/Legends|Trailing Sectors]].<ref name="TEA" />

In [[3963 BBY]], Myrkr was the site of [[Battle of Myrkr (Mandalorian Wars)|fighting]] during the [[Mandalorian Wars]]. Myrkr was settled by [[Human/Legends|Humans]] circa [[300 BBY/Legends|300 BBY]]. During the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], many [[Pirate/Legends|pirates]], criminals, and [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunters]] hid on Myrkr because the [[Ysalamiri/Legends|ysalamiri]] were avoided by the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] and it was a perfect place for a base of operations because the high metal content of the flora confused most sensor equipment. Despite its relatively central location, Myrkr was generally ignored by galactic society during the time of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. The guardian of [[Nomi Sunrider]]'s [[Holocron/Legends|holocron]] was known to be from the race that inhabited Myrkr.

[[File:Myrkr_Base.jpg|thumb|right|250px|[[Talon Karrde]]'s [[Myrkr Base|base]] on Myrkr.]]
Myrkr was home to the ysalamiri, creatures which created bubbles which pushed back [[The Force/Legends|the Force]].<ref name="TCSWE" /> This ability evolved to protect them from pack animals called [[vornskr]]s, the only known animals to hunt exclusively by sensing the Force. The ysalamiri lived on [[olbio tree]]s.

During the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], the [[Zann Consortium/Legends|Zann Consortium]] may have infiltrated the planet. The Consortium possibly gained the ability to train vornskrs and build [[ysalamiri cage]]s for their [[Mobile Defense Unit]]s.

In [[9 ABY/Legends|9 ABY]], Myrkr was located between Imperial and [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] territory. During that time, [[Talon Karrde]]'s organization had a [[Myrkr Base|base]] on Myrkr. In the early phases of [[Grand Admiral/Legends|Grand Admiral]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo/Legends|Thrawn's]] campaign, Imperial forces moved on the world in order to [[Rescue on Myrkr|secure]] supplies of ysalamiri.

The [[Yuuzhan Vong]] conquered the planet and used the native vornskrs to create the [[voxyn]], which were cloned in the [[Koros-Strohna|worldship]] ''[[Baanu Rass]]'' in the [[Myrkr system/Legends|Myrkr system]]. A [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Myrkr strike team|strike team]] [[Mission to Myrkr|infiltrated]] this worldship to kill the voxyn queen. During this mission, [[Anakin Solo]] was killed. After the mission, ''Baanu Rass'' was destroyed, and the [[Domain Lah worldship]] went into orbit over Myrkr.

During the [[Second Galactic Civil War]], [[Darth Caedus|Jacen Solo]] brought [[Tahiri Veila]] to the system in order to use his abilities in [[flow-walking]] to revisit the Myrkr mission. Although Jacen claimed his intentions were noble, he was in fact manipulating Tahiri so that she would become more and more loyal to him and him alone. The two watched the final moments of the mission and Tahiri was able to give Anakin one last kiss before he succumbed to his wounds. So addicted to flow-walking was Tahiri that the two revisited the scene a further five times, tiring Jacen but completely bending her to his will.

==Inhabitants==
Apart from the native [[Neti/Legends|Neti]] species Myrkr's population consisted of [[Human/Legends|Human]] settlers of which most of them were mainly outlaws (smugglers, malcontents, and fugitives from other worlds), who primarily used the planet's obscurity for smuggling operations and other illegal activities.<ref name="EGPM" /><ref name="TCSWE" /> One such particular smuggler was [[Talon Karrde]], who, during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], placed his smuggling organization's secret [[Myrkr Base|headquarters]] deep inside Myrkr's [[Great Northern Forest]].<ref name="EGPM" />

==Behind the scenes==
On numerous occasions, the [[Star Wars: The New Jedi Order|''New Jedi Order'' series]] of books has misspelled Myrkr as "Mukyr."
